page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r6.xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual server instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at 2.5 GHz. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage and featuring a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the ecs.r6.xlarge exhibits modest processing capabilities. In stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests, the instance scores in the bottom 25% tier. Similarly, single-threaded gzip compression and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression fall into the weak and poor performance categories respectively. Memory performance is mixed; while the PassMark memory score reaches the middle 50% average tier, uncached large-block read and write memory bandwidth benchmarks remain in the bottom 25%.

From a qualitative perspective, the instance provides a high density of RAM relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require high CPU throughput. Database operations and Redis SET benchmarks perform in the bottom 25%, indicating that while the instance can host caching layers or database instances, it is limited by its processing speed. Appropriate workloads include memory-intensive applications, caching layers, and general-purpose tasks requiring a larger memory footprint than standard compute instances.
